title: PARK THE MEMORY FOR SUPPORTED CARE
name: PARK THE MEMORY FOR SUPPORTED CARE
ritual_name: PARK THE MEMORY FOR SUPPORTED CARE
goal: Stop reopening the memory and move it toward supported care.
steps:
1. Stop adding sensory detail or searching for meaning.
2. Choose a qualified professional or safe appointment for later support.
3. Say one short reminder that the topic needs supported care.
4. End the reminder without reopening the memory.
5. Return attention to a neutral task in the current environment.

title: BUILD A PRESENT-DAY SAFETY MAP
name: BUILD A PRESENT-DAY SAFETY MAP
goal: Build a short present-day safety map you can actually use.
steps:
1. Name two present-day supports that can actually be reached.
2. Name one familiar place where you feel more present and steady.
3. Identify a practical exit from the current stressful setting.
4. Choose the person or service to contact if steadiness drops.
5. Keep the short map in mind and avoid adding memory content.

title: COUNT WHAT IS STILL HERE
name: COUNT WHAT IS STILL HERE
goal: Break scarcity vision by seeing what is still available before deciding what is missing.
steps:
1. Name the shortage your mind is zoomed in on.
2. Find three resources already present: time, skill, support, money, options, or information.
3. Pick the one resource that can affect the problem now.
4. Use it once before searching for more.
numberedSteps:

3. Pick the one resource that can affect the problem now.

win: The shortage stayed real, but one usable resource re-entered the picture and created a next move.

title: CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS
name: CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS
goal: Shorten the delay between noticing distraction and returning to the anchor.
steps:
1. Choose an anchor and notice the precise moment contact breaks.
2. Instead of judging the distraction, shorten the delay before returning.
3. Track the interval between noticing and reconnection.
4. Let practice end after one stretch with visibly fewer or shorter gaps.

name: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
goal: Break a night-time storyline into unrelated images that cannot easily continue the plot.
steps:

title: THE ACTION HAD MANY AUTHORS
name: THE ACTION HAD MANY AUTHORS
goal: See how your action was shaped by you and by the conditions around you.
steps:
1. Review one action. Name what shaped it: intention, habit, body, other people, resources, timing, culture, and chance.
2. Put yourself among those causes, not above them.
3. Keep responsibility for your part without claiming you caused everything.

title: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
name: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
ritual_name: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
goal: Make an intentionally imperfect start, repair one useful part, and stop polishing.
steps:
1. Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.
2. Imagine one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy first sentence, rough title, rough mental outline, or unfinished opening.
3. Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest.
4. Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise keep the corrected fragment in mind and stop cleanly.

title: SOFT DELIVERY, SOLID MESSAGE
name: SOFT DELIVERY, SOLID MESSAGE
goal: Keep the message firm while removing unnecessary attack from its delivery.
steps:
1. Remove attacks from your wording.
2. Show one sign of genuine interest, validate the understandable part of the other experience, and use an easy rather than contemptuous manner.
3. Keep your core message unchanged.
4. Gentleness edits delivery, not truth.

title: THE EMOTION LINEUP
name: THE EMOTION LINEUP
goal: Check whether the first emotion you named is the one your body is actually signalling.
steps:
1. Say the first emotion name that comes to mind.
2. Check the body clues: heat, heaviness, tightness, energy, urge, and location.
3. Compare three nearby labels, such as angry, hurt, scared, ashamed, or disappointed.
4. Choose the label that best fits the clues, then notice whether the next action becomes clearer.

goal: Say the unsent truth in your mind, then leave contact alone for a full day.

title: THE TWENTY-MINUTE TRUTH STORY
name: THE TWENTY-MINUTE TRUTH STORY
goal: Tell the truth in a contained window and finish by returning to today.
steps:
1. Choose up to twenty minutes.
2. In your mind, move through what occurred, what you felt, and what it means now.
3. End by naming your location, today’s date, and one caring action you can take.
4. Try again on another day only if it helps.

title: TURN ANTICIPATION INTO INVENTORY
name: TURN ANTICIPATION INTO INVENTORY
goal: Convert repeated future scenes into preparation until they stop producing anything new.
steps:
1. Each time the same future scene repeats, extract one actionable item: question, document, rehearsal, route, support, or if-then link.
2. Add it to a checklist.
3. When repetition yields no new preparation, stamp the simulation PAID IN FULL and switch to execution.

title: BODY SIGNAL, STORY LATER
name: BODY SIGNAL, STORY LATER
goal: Notice one ordinary part of your life as if you had just regained access to it.
steps:
1. Imagine briefly that you lost access to your current life and then unexpectedly got it back.
2. Notice what small thing would suddenly matter: someone’s voice, a body ability, unfinished work, or morning light.
3. Do one thing today that honours that value without pretending real hardship is okay.

name: COOL THE WORDS, KEEP THE FACTS
ritual_name: COOL THE WORDS, KEEP THE FACTS
goal: Replace inflammatory language with the exact frequency, loss, or behaviour it refers to.
steps:

3. Say the cooler version once and notice what action it supports.

title: LOOK FOR THE MISSING DANGER
name: LOOK FOR THE MISSING DANGER
goal: Look once for the sign that should be present if the feared model is right.
steps:
1. Ask what sign must exist right now if the feared model is correct.
2. Search once, fairly.
3. If it is absent, keep that absence and reduce—not erase—the model’s weight.
4. Name the alternate explanation strengthened by the missing sign.

title: THREE ACTIVE FUTURES ONLY
name: THREE ACTIVE FUTURES ONLY
goal: Keep only three future possibilities active enough to affect the decision.
steps:
1. Pick the three future possibilities that matter most right now.
2. A new one can enter only if it replaces, combines with, or clearly beats one already there.
3. Remove the retired possibility from your mental board.
4. Decide from the three that remain.

title: VIVID IS NOT IMPORTANT
name: VIVID IS NOT IMPORTANT
goal: Separate how noticeable information feels from how much it actually changes the decision.
steps:
1. Score the information on two separate axes: how noticeable it feels and how much it changes the choice.
2. A dramatic item with low relevance pays a felt importance tax and moves down the priority list.
3. Allocate attention to decision impact instead.

title: STAMP THE ENDING INTO THE SENSES
name: STAMP THE ENDING INTO THE SENSES
ritual_name: STAMP THE ENDING INTO THE SENSES
goal: Give a truly finished topic one repeatable sensory ending and a clear return time.
steps:
1. Choose one finish you can repeat: wash your hands, hear a soft sound, touch a doorframe, or change the light.
2. Pair it with one short answer in your mind and a time to think about it again.
3. Use the sensory finish only when the topic is truly closed.

45–60 seconds

GOAL
Track whether an emotion is rising, steady, or falling before acting from its intensity.

STEPS
1. At three intervals, keep not only level but direction and speed: rising fast, steady, falling slowly.
2. Add the action impulse at each point.
3. Make decisions from trajectory plus facts, not from the first intensity number alone.

WIN
Three readings showed level, direction, speed, and action urge, so the decision used the whole trajectory.

MIND BEND
Intensity is only a snapshot. A high feeling already falling may call for a different response than a lower feeling accelerating.

FORMULA FLOW
Set Level → Add Action → Make Decisions

SAFETY
PAUSE
Escalating risk calls for support before further tracking.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

title: CHANGE THE RHYTHM, CHANGE THE STATE
name: CHANGE THE RHYTHM, CHANGE THE STATE
ritual_name: CHANGE THE RHYTHM, CHANGE THE STATE
goal: Change the pace of speech, movement, or breathing and watch what emotional state follows.
steps:
1. Notice the cadence of speech, movement, or breathing.
2. Choose an opposite rhythm: agitated becomes deliberate, collapsed becomes lightly brisk, looping becomes irregular.
3. Maintain the new tempo through one simple task and observe the emotional shift.

name: TRAIT OR OLD PROTECTION STRATEGY?
goal: Treat a disliked trait as a protection strategy and test a cheaper way to get the same safety.
steps:
1. Choose the disliked trait.
2. Ask what threat it once reduced and what payoff maintains it now.
3. Design one alternative strategy that offers the same protection with lower cost.
4. Test it in a low-stakes situation before rewriting identity.

title: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
name: ENTER THROUGH A RANDOM DOOR
goal: Let a random workable section choose the starting point when order does not matter.
steps:
1. Name three to six task sections that can safely be done in any order and give each one a number.
2. Let the first number that pops into your mind choose the section. Do not pick again just because you dislike it.
3. Work only inside that section for ninety seconds; do not reorganise the whole project.
4. Notice one concrete sign of progress, then decide whether to choose another number or close.

title: LEAVE A BRIDGE BACK

title: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
name: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
ritual_name: CHOOSE THE EASIEST MISTAKE TO CATCH
goal: Prefer the option whose failure becomes visible while correction is still practical.
steps:
1. Name the two or three live options. For each, picture the specific way it could fail—not a vague fear.
2. Name the earliest visible sign that failure has begun. It must be visible or clear, not a feeling alone.
3. State what corrective action would still be available when that sign appears and what cost has already accumulated.
4. Choose the option whose reliable warning arrives while correction is still practical. Use this as one decision criterion, not the whole verdict.

title: SORT THE SOUNDS BY DISTANCE

steps:

goal: Compare options on relevant traits before reconnecting them to their emotionally loaded names.
steps:

PLAY TIME
45–60 seconds

GOAL
Group tasks by the kind of attention they require and stay in one brain mode at a time.

name: WHAT KIND OF EFFORT IS THIS?
ritual_name: WHAT KIND OF EFFORT IS THIS?
goal: Identify what kind of effort you are feeling before deciding that effort means failure.
steps:
1. Classify the strain using evidence.
2. If danger, stop; if novelty, allow learning; if skill growth, dose it; if poor design, simplify the system.
3. Respond to the category instead of interpreting all effort as failure.

goal: Notice both the thing perceived and the act of perceiving without making either side the whole story.

3. Refuse to place all reality on either side.
4. Let seeing or hearing itself become primary for several seconds.

title: START INSIDE THE CLOCK
name: START INSIDE THE CLOCK
goal: Test a realistic work duration against the clock and stop after one clear change.
steps:
1. Pick a realistic amount of time.
2. Check two likely durations.
3. Work only with the next minute.
4. Complete the smallest timed piece.
5. Stop after one clear change.

State the request as a request, lower the tone, and let the answer arrive before interpretation.

Practical support was named plainly and one complete response entered without being interrupted by your prediction.

Requests become easier to answer when they are not asked to carry the hidden burden of proving what the other person thinks.

title: LISTEN BEFORE THE REPLY ARRIVES
name: LISTEN BEFORE THE REPLY ARRIVES
goal: Let the full statement arrive, check its meaning, and answer with the smallest honest sentence.
steps:

2. Stay with a full statement without interrupting it.
3. Check their meaning before replying.
4. Leave room for one missing fact.
5. Use the smallest honest sentence.

full_consumer_ritual:
PLAY TIME
60–120 seconds

GOAL
Carry uncertainty openly while giving the team one immediate focus and a factual update.

STEPS
1. Notice what the team needs from you even while you are still uncertain.
2. Name what remains uncertain.
3. Choose the team's immediate focus.
4. Give a brief fact-and-impact update.
5. Review only what changed after the update.

WIN
What remained unknown was named without blocking one clear team priority and one review of what actually changed.

MIND BEND
Uncertainty can travel safely through a team when it is labelled. Hidden uncertainty often reappears as inconsistent direction.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Evidence → Name Unknown → Name Focus → Post Brief → Review Once

PAUSE

title: LIVING EDGE, CLEAN EXIT
name: LIVING EDGE, CLEAN EXIT
goal: Accept what already happened without turning acceptance into approval.
steps:
1. Name what happened without changing whether it was right or wrong.
2. Say, “Accepting that it happened is not approving it.”
3. Notice what energy is being spent fighting the fact that it already occurred.
4. Choose one boundary, repair, or next action that still belongs to you.
5. Let the event remain unacceptable if it was unacceptable, while releasing the demand that reality be different.

STEPS
1. Step away from traffic, heights, weapons, substances, or conflict.
2. Choose a quieter known place without driving yourself there.
3. Tell someone clearly that you cannot slow down safely.
4. Use emergency or crisis support from the Safety section.
5. Stay with support until a professional can assess you.

WIN
You reached a lower-risk setting and stayed with support until professional assessment began.

MIND BEND
When your body is too highly charged for safe judgement, reducing hazards matters more than understanding why. The environment can carry safety temporarily.

FORMULA FLOW
Exit Area → Lower Stimulation → Tell Human → Contact Help → Wait Supported

SAFETY
PAUSE
IMMEDIATE DANGER OR POSSIBLE MEDICAL EMERGENCY: call Triple Zero (000) now.
24/7 CRISIS SUPPORT: call Lifeline 13 11 14 or text 0477 13 11 14.
Stay with a safe person and follow qualified support. Do not return to ordinary rituals.

goal: Let an intrusive thought exist without treating its arrival as a message.
steps:

4. Do that ordinary thing for ten seconds without checking whether the thought is gone.

45–90 seconds

GOAL
Let an intrusive thought exist without treating its arrival as a message.

STEPS
1. Say, “A thought showed up.”
2. Add, “Showing up is not a message.”
3. Name one ordinary thing in front of you that has nothing to do with the thought.
4. Do that ordinary thing for ten seconds without checking whether the thought is gone.

WIN
The thought stayed unanswered while attention moved into an ordinary object and action unrelated to it.

MIND BEND
A thought's appearance tells you that the brain produced it. It does not automatically tell you why, what it means, or what deserves action.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Arrival → Remove Message → Pick Ordinary → Continue Ten

SAFETY
PAUSE
Stop if this makes you less steady, more distressed, or less able to act safely. Use human, professional, medical, or emergency support when the situation needs more than self-help.
This brief reset is not diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.
